q: Under DAEDS (Sec. 6.1.1), how is the contracting arrangement structured?
o: A single contract between the Architect and the Owner, with sub-consultancy contracts between the Architect and the other professionals
No written contract is required; a verbal agreement suffices
Separate contracts between the Owner and each of the engineering and allied professionals
A single contract between the Owner and each engineer, with the Architect as sub-consultant
n: DAEDS uses a single contract between the Architect and the Owner; the Architect then engages the other professionals under separate sub-consultancy contracts. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1.1)

q: What is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) under Group IV?
n: Group IV's DAEDS rate — covering both architectural and engineering design under a single Architect-held contract — is a flat 10% of Project Construction Cost. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4)

q: What DAEDS fee applies under the flat Group IV rate?
scenario: Scenario: A row-house development (Group IV) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 25,000,000.

q: Because Group IV's rate is flat rather than a graduated bracket (unlike Groups I-III, where the percentage decreases and a base amount is added once PCC exceeds P100 million), what DAEDS fee applies to this residence?
o: The Group IV rate does not apply once PCC exceeds P100 million
A reduced rate applies above P100 million, giving a lower fee than 10% of PCC
PHP 3,900,000, following the Group I DAEDS bracket for PCC over P100 million
PHP 12,000,000 — still 10% of the full PCC, since Group IV has no bracket table
n: Group IV has no bracket table — the 10% DAEDS rate applies uniformly to the entire PCC no matter how large the project is. RPF = 0.10 x PHP 120,000,000 = PHP 12,000,000. (Sec. 6.3.4 (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6))
scenario: Scenario: A large, high-end single-detached residence (Group IV) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 120,000,000.

q: A developer is designing a high-rise residential condominium tower. Under the SPP Doc. 202 building groups, which group governs this project's fee rather than Group IV?
o: There is no applicable group; condominiums use a separate fee schedule entirely
Group 2 — Residential Condominiums are listed under Group 2, not Group IV
Group IV, since it is still a residential building
n: "Residential Condominiums" appear explicitly under Group 2 (buildings of moderate complexity), not Group IV — Group IV is limited to single-detached/duplex houses, row-/shop-houses, small apartment houses, and townhouses. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.2 (Group 2) cf. Sec. 6.3.4 (Group IV))

q: A client building a single-detached family home wants one architectural firm to be fully accountable for coordinating structural, electrical, and sanitary/plumbing engineering under one umbrella agreement, rather than hiring engineers directly. Which manner of providing services should the Architect propose?
o: DAEDS — a single contract with the Architect, who then sub-consults the engineers
DADS — separate contracts between the Owner and each engineer
n: Because the client wants a single point of contract accountability covering both architectural and engineering design, DAEDS is appropriate: the Architect signs one contract with the Owner and sub-consults the engineering and allied professionals. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1.1)

q: Under SPP Document 202, what is the title of Sec. 6, which contains the building-group fee schedules?
n: Sec. 6 of SPP Doc. 202 is titled "Regular Design Services"; it sets out the manner of providing services, the methods of compensation, and the building-group fee tables (including Group IV, residences). (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6)

q: Whether services are provided under DAEDS or DADS, how are the professional responsibilities and civil liabilities of the Architect and the other State-regulated professionals treated?
o: They remain separate — the Architect does not assume the responsibilities and liabilities of the other professionals
The Architect assumes full liability for all professionals under DAEDS only
Liability is always shared jointly and severally among all professionals
The Owner assumes all professional liability once the contract is signed
n: In both DAEDS and DADS, each State-regulated professional's responsibility and civil liability remains separate; the Architect does not assume the liabilities of the other professionals (RLPs). (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1)

q: What is the Recommended Professional Fee (RPF) for Detailed Architectural Design Services (DADS) under Group IV?
n: Group IV's DADS rate — where the Architect's contract covers architectural design only, with the Owner separately contracting the engineers — is a flat 6% of Project Construction Cost. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4)

q: How does the Group IV Recommended Professional Fee structure differ from that of Groups I–III?
o: Group IV and Groups I–III both use identical bracket tables

Group IV uses a single flat percentage of PCC for each service (10% DAEDS / 6% DADS) regardless of project cost, while Groups I–III use graduated bracket tables that add a percentage of the excess over cost thresholds
Group IV fees are computed per square meter, while Groups I–III use percentage of PCC
Group IV uses graduated brackets while Groups I–III use flat percentages
n: Unlike Groups I, II, and III, which scale the RPF through bracket tables (a base peso amount plus a percentage of the excess PCC beyond a threshold), Group IV simply applies one flat percentage to the entire PCC, with no bracket table. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4 cf. Secs. 6.3.1-6.3.3)

q: Under DADS (Sec. 6.1.2), how is the contracting arrangement structured?
o: The Architect sub-contracts all engineering work under one umbrella agreement
The Owner contracts only with the Architect, who is deemed to represent all other professionals
The Architect and the engineering and allied professionals each execute separate contracts directly with the Owner
The Owner and the Architect share a single contract with the engineers as witnesses
n: Under DADS, the Architect and the engineering/allied professionals each execute their own, separate contract directly with the Owner — unlike DAEDS, where the Architect holds a single contract and sub-consults the others. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1.2)

q: For the same PHP 120,000,000 residence, what DADS fee applies?
scenario: Scenario: A large, high-end single-detached residence (Group IV) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 120,000,000.

q: Under Sec. 6.1 (Manner of Providing Services), how many ways may the Architect, as Lead Professional, enter into contract with the Owner together with the engineering and allied professionals?
o: One — a single combined contract only
Three — DAEDS, DADS, and a joint-venture contract
Four, one for each design discipline
n: Sec. 6.1 provides exactly two manners of providing services: Detailed Architectural and Engineering Design Services (DAEDS) and Detailed Architectural Design Services (DADS). (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1)

q: A homeowner planning a duplex has already engaged and separately contracts her own structural engineer and electrical engineer directly, and only wants the Architect to handle the detailed architectural design. Which service manner and Group IV fee rate applies to the Architect's engagement?
n: Since the Owner is directly and separately contracting the engineers herself, the Architect's engagement is DADS (Detailed Architectural Design Services), for which Group IV's flat rate is 6% of PCC. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1.2 and Sec. 6.3.4)

q: A cluster of attached homes sharing common walls, sold or built along a street frontage as individual units, is best described in Group IV terminology as:
o: A Group VI repetitive-construction housing project only
Row-houses (or shop-houses, if ground-floor commercial space is included)
n: Group IV expressly lists row-houses and shop-houses (attached units along a frontage, the latter with ground-floor commercial use) as residence types it covers. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4)

q: What is the overall purpose of grouping buildings into Groups (e.g., Group I through Group IX and beyond) under Sec. 6.3?
o: To assign buildings to different professional regulatory boards
To determine fair remuneration for the Architect based on the degree of complexity and creative skill a building type requires
To determine which buildings require a building permit
To rank buildings by required floor area for zoning purposes
n: Sec. 6.3 explains that architectural work is classified according to the degree of complexity and creative skill needed to meet the Client's requirements, and this grouping is used to determine fair remuneration for the Architect. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3)

q: Using the Group IV DADS rate for the same project, what is the Recommended Professional Fee if the Architect is instead engaged under DADS?
n: RPF (DADS) = 6% x PCC = 0.06 x PHP 2,300,000 = PHP 138,000. (Sec. 6.3.4 (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6))
scenario: Scenario: An Architect is engaged to design a single-detached residence with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 2,300,000.

q: A townhouse development (Group IV) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 48,750,000, and the Owner engages the Architect under DAEDS. What is the Recommended Professional Fee?
Applying the Group IV DAEDS rate, what is the Recommended Professional Fee?
scenario: Scenario: A row of shop-houses (ground-floor retail with upper-floor residential units) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 8,400,000.

q: For a Group IV residence with a PCC of PHP 15,000,000, how much more would the Owner pay in professional fees by engaging the Architect under DAEDS instead of DADS?
n: DAEDS fee = 10% x 15,000,000 = PHP 1,500,000; DADS fee = 6% x 15,000,000 = PHP 900,000; difference = PHP 1,500,000 - PHP 900,000 = PHP 600,000. The extra 4% compensates the Architect for holding the single contract and coordinating the sub-consulted engineers directly. (Sec. 6.3.4 (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6))

q: Per Sec. 6.3.4, which building types fall under Group IV?
o: Industrial plants, warehouses, and parking structures
Residences (single-detached, single-attached or duplex; row-houses or shop-houses), small apartment houses and townhouses
Monumental buildings requiring consummate design skill and precise detailing
Office buildings, banks, schools, and shopping centers
n: Group IV covers residences — single-detached, single-attached or duplex houses; row-houses or shop-houses — as well as small apartment houses and townhouses. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4)

q: Under Group IV, what DAEDS fee should the Architect propose for this duplex?
scenario: Scenario: A duplex (single-attached) residence has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 5,000,000.

q: The 10% of PCC (DAEDS) and 6% of PCC (DADS) rates for Group IV fall under which method of compensation listed in Sec. 6.2?
o: 6.2.5 — Per Diem, Honorarium Plus Reimbursable Expenses
n: The Group IV rates are expressed as a percentage of Project Construction Cost, i.e., compensation method 6.2.1, one of the several methods (unit cost, fee plus expenses, lump sum, per diem, DPE multiple, mixed) listed under Sec. 6.2. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.2.1)

q: Under Group IV, what DADS fee should the Architect propose for this same duplex?
scenario: Scenario: A duplex (single-attached) residence has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 5,000,000.

q: What DADS fee applies under the flat Group IV rate for the same row-house development?
scenario: Scenario: A row-house development (Group IV) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 25,000,000.

q: An Architect is engaged under DAEDS for a townhouse project, and the sub-consulted structural engineer commits a design error that damages a unit. Under Sec. 6.1, who bears the civil liability for that error?
o: The structural engineer alone — professional responsibility and liability remain separate even under DAEDS
The Owner, since the Owner ultimately pays for all services
The Architect alone, since DAEDS places the Architect as the sole party of the single contract
Liability is shared equally between the Architect and the Owner
n: Sec. 6.1 makes clear that in both DAEDS and DADS, each State-regulated professional's responsibility and civil liability remains separate; the Architect does not assume the liabilities of the sub-consulted engineers merely because DAEDS routes payment through a single contract. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.1)

q: Besides single-detached, single-attached/duplex, and row-/shop-houses, what two other residential building types are explicitly named under Group IV?
n: Group IV's coverage, as stated in Sec. 6.3.4, closes with "small apartment houses and townhouses," in addition to the detached/duplex and row-/shop-house types. (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.4)

q: Using the Group IV DAEDS rate, what is the Recommended Professional Fee if the Architect is engaged under DAEDS?
n: RPF (DAEDS) = 10% x PCC = 0.10 x PHP 2,300,000 = PHP 230,000. (Sec. 6.3.4 (SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6))
scenario: Scenario: An Architect is engaged to design a single-detached residence with a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 2,300,000.

q: Applying the Group IV DADS rate to the same shop-house row, what is the Recommended Professional Fee?
scenario: Scenario: A row of shop-houses (ground-floor retail with upper-floor residential units) has a Project Construction Cost (PCC) of PHP 8,400,000.
